conflicts.fact: The mkokoteni's acceleration down the Limuru escarpment (and the value of g used) differs between lessons, so the cart's speeds and distances are incompatible.
conflicts.versions: L2: a = 2 m/s² (12 m/s and 36 m at 6 s; 16 m/s at 8 s), gravity ≈ 2 m/s² along slope. L3: a = 2.5 m/s², 20 m/s and 80 m after 8 s. L4: a = g = 9.8 m/s² (29.4 m/s and 44.1 m after 3 s). L5: a = g = 10 m/s² (50 m/s at 5 s, 125 m). L7: a = 10 m/s². L8: a ≈ 3 m/s², reaching about 40 m/s (144 km/h).

conflicts.fact: Mkokoteni speed after 8 s is also internally inconsistent within L3, and L3's 20 m/s and 80 m is not the same as what the other lessons imply.
conflicts.versions: L3 gives a = 2.5 m/s² with t = 8 s as 20 m/s and 80 m (L3 uses g = 10 m/s² for free fall), while L5 has the cart at 50 m/s after 5 s on the same road.

conflicts.fact: Value of g used for free fall differs.
conflicts.versions: L4: g = 9.8 m/s² (accepted value). L3, L5, L8: g = 10 m/s². L5 says 'a = g' for the slope, while L8 says only a slope component acts (3 m/s²).

conflicts.fact: Whether the cart on the slope accelerates at g or less than g.
conflicts.versions: L4 and L5 say the cart accelerates at g (L4: 'including our mkokoteni'; L5: a = g = 10 m/s² down the slope). L8 says the cart's acceleration is only about 3 m/s² because only a component of gravity acts along the slope, and g applies only in vertical free fall.

conflicts.fact: Cart's speed at the crash point / distances along the road.
conflicts.versions: L5: v ≈ 100 m/s (360 km/h) at 500 m, 50 m/s at 125 m. L8: about 40 m/s (144 km/h) at the crash point; v ≈ 34.6 m/s at 200 m. L5 also describes Point B (125 m) as ~5 s, and Point C (500 m) as ~10 s, which gives 100 m/s, not matching L8.

conflicts.fact: Which kinematic equations are used / how many.
conflicts.versions: L5 uses three simplified equations (v = at, s = ½at², v² = 2as) and L6 lists three equations, while L2, L3, L7, L8 refer to four equations of linear motion.
L1 defines it as the continuous speed increase / rate of change of velocity; L2 says 'acceleration means a constant change in velocity', adding constancy to the definition.

conflicts.fact: Mkokoteni's relation to braking/ability to stop.
conflicts.versions: L3 and L6 discuss the cart stopping with brakes ('if the mkokoteni had brakes'), while L7 says the cart had NO brakes at all; L6 braking a = −8 m/s².
